Subject: AvaHealth perf: SLO scenarios & token tradeoffs (post-demo)

Hi Emily / Samir —

Thanks again for taking the demo today. Short recap and the concrete asks we discussed so we can scope a short perf POC. Important context: the ask centers on the clinical summarization flow (input-heavy) and the patient-facing explanation flow (output-heavy / streaming).

Key SLOs you mentioned on the call:
- Interactive summarization (clinician UI): target p95 latency <= 400 ms for up to 1k input tokens and up to 250 output tokens; expected baseline concurrency ~= 10 sessions.
- Patient explanation (chat-like): streaming required for outputs up to 1,500 tokens; target first-token latency <= 300 ms and tail latency p95 <= 1.2 s when streaming.
- Bulk nightly batch reports: throughput target ~200 reqs/min, latency not strict but we want cost-optimal profiles.

Context window and token distribution notes (tangible asks):
- Typical clinical note size: 2k-6k tokens (we'll provide samples). Most summarization uses ~1k of the recent context + 200-300 tokens of anchor notes.
- Patient messages are usually short inputs (<128 tokens) but outputs can be long (up to 1,500 tokens) and must stream progressively to the UI.

Latency impact summary (what we discussed):
- Long input context increases KV cache memory pressure and raises per-token generation cost roughly linearly once you exceed the model's optimal cache sizing. That tends to push tail p95 up if not mitigated.
- Output-heavy flows (long beams/long samplings) blow up GPU compute time per request and can increase queuing under concurrency. Streaming helps perceived latency (first token) but keeps the request pinned until generation completes, tying up slots.
- Batching reduces unit cost but increases first-token latency; continuous batching with small time budgets is usually the best trade for mixed interactive workloads.

Suggested next steps for a short POC (2 weeks):
1) You share a set of 20 representative prompt pairs (we asked for sample_prompts.jsonl) and a traffic shape (concurrency histogram).
2) We run two profiles: (A) interactive optimized: continuous batching + KV caching, target p95 <=400ms for the summarization scenario; (B) streaming optimized: streaming low-latency first token + model variant for long outputs, target first-token <=300ms and p95 tail <=1.2s.
3) We'll exercise fallback rules: model-quantized variants (8-bit), and an accelerated streaming path with prefix caching.
4) Post-test deliverables: per-scenario p50/p95/p99, token-cost estimates, recommended deployment config (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private).

I attached an initial workbook (AVA_Perf_Scenarios.xlsx) with the high-level test matrix and a proposed mutual action plan. Can you confirm the sample set and whether the batch windows (they said 11pm-3am local) are accurate? Also confirm whether HIPAA controls require Private deployment for any POC data (we offered a masked-data option on Hosted).

Thanks — planning to slot the perf run early next week if we get samples.

Best,

2) For the patient-facing chat, streaming is a hard requirement; first-token perception matters more than full completion latency. If you can deliver an option to stream the first 1–2 tokens within ~200–300ms we'll be happy.
3) HIPAA: POC data will be de-identified, but for long-term we will require Private deployment. For the POC please assume masked PHI is acceptable on Hosted.

Looping in a couple of quick tech constraints and options so Marissa can set expectations: 

- Rolling-window prefix trimming: we can emulate prioritizing the last 1k tokens by constructing the prompt at the client (recommended) or at the gateway (we can implement a rolling-window preprocessor in the POC). Gateway trimming reduces token count but doesn't save compute that arises from long KV cache warming unless we also enable cache reuse.

- Streaming slot saturation: two practical fallbacks: (A) hedged routing to a quantized streaming variant (8-bit/4-bit Q), and (B) an early-termination policy that streams the first N tokens as a preview, then continues generation offline and posts the remainder to the UI. Option A maintains interactive feel with lower compute cost; Option B reduces concurrency pressure at the expense of additional UX plumbing.

- Model choices: for summarization we recommend a larger context-aware model with KV caching. For patient messages, use a lower-latency variant for first-token streaming and switch to a larger variant if longer generation is requested (model cascade). We'll need to measure memory usage for 6k context windows on the candidate GPU (A100/RTX 6000 equivalent) to pick the right quant/profile.

I'll prepare a short test harness plan (traffic replay + synthetic concurrency ramp + streaming slot exhaustion test) and drop into the Drive link. If Marissa wants, Ben and I can run an initial microbenchmark before the full POC to validate the streaming-first-token path.

-Priyom
